samples.summary: DurableYorkieProvider never closes the WafflebaseDocStore it creates — one leaked IndexedDB connection per document opened
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId, ... }), [userId])` (lines 135–176) is the only place this store is constructed, and the component has no `useEffect(() => () => store.close(), [store])`. `WafflebaseDocStore.open()` memoizes an `IDBDatabase` connection on first use and `close()` is the only thing that releases it. Every durable document a user opens in a session therefore leaves an open IndexedDB connection (and its `touched` set) alive for the lifetime of the tab; the store is also swapped without closing when `userId` changes, since `useMemo` just drops the old value. Contrast `OfflineRuntime` (components/offline-runtime.tsx:196), which does call `store.close()` in its effect cleanup, and every helper in `offline-erase.ts`, which closes in `finally`.

samples.summary: The fallback store created by watchForOfflineDisable is never closed
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` then `void eraseOfflineData(current, who).catch(...)`. When the fallback branch is taken (the documented case: the toggle switched off from the Settings route), a brand-new store is constructed, opens a connection, and is never `close()`d — unlike `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, `purgeOfflineDocuments`, `retryPendingOfflineErase` and `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`, all of which close in `finally`. Leaks a connection per off-toggle and keeps a handle open that a later `deleteDatabase`/version change has to negotiate around.

samples.summary: purgeOfflineDocuments aborts the whole batch on the first failing document, silently leaving the rest on disk
samples.evidence: The `for (const id of documentIds) { await store.purgeDocument(...) }` loop sits *inside* a single `try { ... } catch { console.warn }`. A throw while purging the first id (a blocked open, an aborted transaction) skips every remaining id and nothing retries — the caller (`deleteDocuments` in api/documents.ts:214, `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` in api/workspaces.ts:136,167) has already had its server-side deletion accepted, so those documents' full local copies survive until the thirty-day sweep with no record that cleanup was owed. Compare `retryPendingOfflineErase`, which deliberately puts the try/catch *inside* its loop so one failure does not cancel the others.

samples.summary: The call-site durability lapse falls through to "another-tab" for causes that are not another tab (no identity, PDF document)
samples.evidence: `const lapse = decided?.durable ? undefined : !supportsClientKey() ? 'unsupported' : !permitted ? 'not-permitted' : !offlineEnabled ? 'not-enabled' : 'another-tab'`. The chain has no arm for the two other reasons `useDurableDocument` refuses: `!userId` (no resolved identity — `person` undefined, the anonymous/expired case) and `isExcluded(docKey)` (a `pdf-` document, use-durable-document.ts:40). Both land on `'another-tab'`, so the tooltip tells the user "This document is open in another tab, and that tab is the one saving it to this device" when no other tab exists — the opposite of the design requirement quoted in sync-status-tooltip.ts that the tooltip "must name which case applies". Wrong, actionable-looking diagnosis on a state the feature exists to explain.

samples.summary: standDown() performs the lock release as a side effect inside a setState updater
deniedIds() and pendingErases() disagree about how to read a legacy non-array value, so a legacy denial marker is silently dropped
samples.evidence: `pendingErases()` falls through to `return [raw]` when `JSON.parse` yields a non-array (e.g. the bare id `7`, which parses to the number 7 rather than throwing), preserving the documented "one-id spelling". `deniedIds()` has the identical shape but `return []` after the `if (Array.isArray(...))`, and only returns `[raw]` from the `catch`. So a `wafflebase-offline-denied` value that is valid JSON but not an array (a bare number, `null`, an object) reads as "nobody is denied" and `isOfflineWritePermitted` answers `true` — re-permitting local writes for an account whose data was just erased. Narrow (only reachable from a hand-edited or future-format value), but the two functions are written as if they behave the same and do not.

samples.summary: dropArchivesWhere's `onlyUser` parameter is never supplied by any caller, so the scoping it documents never happens
samples.evidence: `private async dropArchivesWhere(index, range, onlyUser?)` builds a `theirs` set to intersect against, but the only two call sites are `dropAllForUser` → `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, IDBKeyRange.only(userId))` (line 1124, already user-scoped by the index) and `collectStale` → `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 1190, deliberately cross-account). The third parameter and the extra `getAllKeys` it would issue are dead. Harmless today, but the JSDoc above it ("`onlyUser` narrows the range … a sweep over `archivedAt` alone would delete another account's") describes a guard that is not in force on the one index that needs it, which is an easy thing for a later reader to rely on.

finding.summary: Swallowing a failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently turns the loss path from "archive the work" into "delete the work" — the comment's claim that this "costs the chip its certainty, never the document" is wrong
finding.evidence: The new `watch()` helper catches a throwing `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...)` and only `console.warn`s. But that handler is the *only* caller of `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())`, and `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771, 791: `const losing = this.expectedLosses.has(documentKey)` / `if (record && losing)`) archives **only** when the latch is set; otherwise it deletes the snapshot, header and change log outright (lines 809-811). The SDK calls `remove()` on the three paths where local work could not be reconciled, so if the pinned SDK (`@yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.22`, per packages/frontend/package.json:99) rejects that event name — the exact scenario the new try/catch was added for — unsent edits are destroyed instead of archived, nothing is ever offered back by `offerRecoverableWork`, and because `reportLoss()` also never fires, `durable` stays true so the chip keeps reading "Saved to this device". That is simultaneously data loss and the over-report the feature says it must never make, with no signal beyond a console warning. If the event is genuinely unsupported the safe behaviour is to degrade the durability claim (e.g. latch `writesFailing`/`persistDisabled`) rather than proceed as if durability held.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed. `watch()` in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:269-278 swallows a throwing `subscribe()` with only a `console.warn`, and it wraps the `local-changes-dropped` subscription (lines 280-285) whose handler is the only production caller of `store.expectLoss()` / `reportLoss()` (grep shows all other `expectLoss` call sites are tests). In WafflebaseDocStore.remove(), the archive `put` is gated on `if (record && losing)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771, 791-803) while the snapshot/header/change-log deletes at 809-811 are unconditional — so a loss-path `remove()` without the latch destroys unsent work with nothing archived. Meanwhile `durable` is `!lost && !writesFailing && !persistDisabled` (line 181) and the catch latches none of them, so the chip keeps claiming "Saved to this device" — the over-report the feature states it must never make. No guard elsewhere makes the catch unreachable: `supportsClientKey()` (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82, MinClientKeyVersion "0.7.23") gates mounting on the @yorkie-js/react pin's `clientKey` prop, not on `Document.subscribe` accepting these event names, and the component's own comment asserts the names can be unsupported at reachable pins (package.json:66,99 pins 0.7.22). Swallowing an error into a silent data-deletion + false-durability state is within the correctness lens (error handling that mis-handles failures, broken invariant, data loss), so it is not out-of-scope. I could not inspect the installed SDK (no node_modules in the tree) to prove the throw impossible, and the try/catch exists for precisely that scenario — uncertainty keeps the finding.
